title: Official Rules
text: Official Rules "UNCOVER THE MUSIC" OFFICIAL RULES / TERMS & CONDITIONS NO PURCHASE NECESSARY HERE'S HOW IT WORKS: MyCoke account holders who visit MyCoke.com can participate in the Uncover the Music game to earn decibels to be added to participant's Decibel account. During each Uncover the Music game, Players will be asked to match pairs of tiles. The more matched pairs that a Player reveals, the more decibels he/she can earn. WHO CAN PLAY: Only registered MyCoke account holders can participate in the Uncover the Music game. Employees of The Coca-Cola Company, Beverage Partners Worldwide (North America), Coca-Cola Bottlers, wholesalers and distributors, their affiliates, subsidiaries, advertising and promotion agencies, redemption/recycling centers, owners/operators and those responsible for making purchasing decisions relative to marketing and promotion of retail establishments that sell Coca-Cola products and the immediate family members and/or those living in same household of each are not eligible. Void where prohibited by law. HOW TO PARTICIPATE IN THE UNCOVER THE MUSIC SAN GAME: There will be various Uncover the Music games going on at the same time. Each Uncover the Music game has a "room" which you must "enter" in order to play that game. To participate in an Uncover the Music game, Players must first enter one of the rooms by clicking on the link for that room. Players can view how many Players are in each room and the V-EGO (screen name) of each Player prior to entering a room. There must be a minimum of 3 Players in a room to start a game, with a maximum of 5 Players per game. The first Player that entered the room decides when to start the game (once there are at least 3 Players in the room, the first Player has 30 seconds to decide when to start the game). The Player to take the first turn will be randomly selected, and Players will continue in a counterclockwise manner. An individual game will include a 24 square grid with 11 matching pairs randomly positioned. During each turn, a Player will click on up to two tiles from the grid. A Player is given 15 seconds to click on up to two tiles; if both tiles are not clicked within this time frame, Player will forfeit his/her turn. After a tile is clicked, it will reveal a pattern that corresponds to a musical accompaniment. (Be sure to turn the volume up on your speakers!) If the patterns on the tiles and their musical accompaniment exactly match, that Player is awarded 1 decibel. Each time a pair of tiles is matched, those tiles are removed from the grid. If a Player matches a pair of tiles, he/she will continue to click up to two more tiles until a match is no longer revealed. Game play will continue until ALL pairs have been matched. Each grid will also include one Wild Card and one Pass Card. (The first time a Wild or Pass Card is revealed, it will be removed from the grid.) The Wild Card allows you to match with any other card. If a Player clicks the Pass Card as the first tile, he/she will not click a second tile, and the next Player in a counterclockwise position begins their turn. If a Player clicks the Pass Card as the second tile, the next Player in a counterclockwise position begins their turn and the first tile remains on the board. If a Player does not reveal a match, the next Player in a counterclockwise position begins their turn to click up to two tiles. The winner is the Player with the highest number of matching pairs in a game and will receive an additional bonus 60 decibels. In the event two or more Players are tied for the most matching pairs at the conclusion of a game, the bonus 60 decibels will be equally split among all tied Players. Decibel account holders can play an Uncover the Music game as many times as they like, however, the maximum number of decibels an account holder can receive playing Uncover the Music is 300 per day (12 midnight - 11:59 p.m.). All decibels earned during an Uncover The Music game will be automatically added to Player's Decibel account immediately upon game completion. In the event a game ends early as a result of Player(s) dropping out thereby reducing the total number of Players to fewer than 3, the game is terminated and all decibels earned at that point will be credited immediately. If a game ends early due to Player dropouts, or for any other reason, the bonus 60 decibels will NOT be awarded. By participating, entrants agree to be bound by Official Rules/Terms and Conditions. Sponsor and judging agency/administrator decisions are final. Sponsor assumes no responsibility for undeliverable emails resulting from any form of active or passive email filtering by a user's internet service provider and/or email client or for insufficient space in user's email account to receive email. Sponsor reserves the right to cancel or modify the promotion if fraud or technical failures destroy the integrity of the promotion; or if a computer virus, bug, or other technical problem corrupts the administration, security, or proper play of the program as determined by Sponsor/judging agency/administrator, in their sole discretion. If the promotion is so canceled, a notice will be posted online and only decibels received as of the date of cancellation will be valid. Sponsors/judging agency/administrator not responsible for typographical errors. In the event of a dispute regardng which specific individual account decibels should be credited to, or which individual is the account holder, the decision will be based on the individual who is the "authorized email account holder." "Authorized email account holder" is defined as the natural person who is assigned to an email address by an Internet access provider, online service provider, or other organization (e.g., business, educational institution etc.) that is responsible for assigning email addresses for the domain associated with the submitted email address. Participant may be requested to provide Sponsor with proof that the participant is the authorized account holder of the email address associated with the account. Any use of robotic, automatic, programmed, or the like methods of participation will void all such submissions by such methods. Sponsor reserves the right to freeze or close an account or to prohibit the participation of an individual/account holder if fraud or tampering is suspected or if the account holder fails to comply with any requirement of participation as stated herein or with any provision in these Official Rules. text: FAQs The Music Pass Earning and Using Decibels Coke Studios Create Your Demo Downloads Send Us Your Feedback The Music Pass: The Music Pass is an important part of the navigation of the site. It is also your ticket (for registered users) to getting into many of the areas within Coke Music. You’ll notice that everywhere you go in Coke Music, the music pass is there. It has links on it to earn decibels, a running tally of your current decibel amount, and a link to the decibel tracker (a kind of decibel checkbook.). The pass also has a picture of your digital self called the V-ego, and a link that allows you to change your V-ego’s look. Back to Top Earning and using Decibels: Decibels are the "currency" that you use in Coke Studios to buy furniture, pictures, and other items for your personal studio. You can earn decibels in several ways: Becoming a member of the site by registering. Creating, performing and getting votes for playing your music in the Coke Studios virtual chat environment. Under the cap when you get a coke in coke studios. Filling out any surveys we occasionally offer up. Other methods will follow as we update the site in the future. Spending decibels requires you to enter the Coke Studios virtual chat environment. The decibels that you have accrued on your badge will automatically show up in your V-ego’s backpack in Coke Studios. You can add furniture and other items into your personal studio by buying them from the online catalogue. Any purchased items will appear in your backpack, and as the owner, you will be able to place it into your personal studio and move it around. Back to Top Coke Studios: Wondering where the new Coke Studios is? We're still working on finishing touches, so we've brought back the "original" Coke Studios until we're done. The new features and venues are still coming your way! If you've given us the OK to email you, we'll let you know when "Coke Studios 2.0" is live. Coke Studios is a combination of virtual chat, music, and fun. When you register, you are taken to a page where you can customize your V-ego — that becomes your digital self. This also becomes the picture you see on your Music Pass. Your V-ego represents how you will appear in the virtual world of Coke Studios. The virtual environment has public areas and personal areas (created by other users). It is really easy to move around when you enter Coke Studios. While you are in a studio just click a spot on the floor to move your V-ego to that spot. You can have a conversation too - just type in what you want to say and it appears in the bubbles above your V-ego. When chatting, you can select to speak normally and other V-egos up to 5 grid units away can hear you (see your bubble), or you can shout by moving the toggle button in the lower left of the screen and everybody in the room will hear (see your bubble). You can also: Dance by pressing the dance button. See another V-ego's public profile by clicking on that V-ego. Sit by clicking on the chair or couch you want to sit on. Drink Cokes. Now for the fun part. Once inside, find the studio mixers placed all over in the personal rooms or public locations on the map. Make your V-ego walk up to the studio mixer and mix some music (This is the same Mixer you’ll find in “Create Your Demo”). Just follow the instructions and have fun. Make sure to burn a virtual CD of any music you want to keep. Your burned CD will show up in your backpack located at the bottom of your screen. Now you are ready to get out there and make the scene. With your CDs (you get 10 for free when you create your personal studio) you can go all over the virtual studio world and play your music for the masses. Why? If other users like your music, they can vote for you, and you earn decibels. You can even make copies and pass them to friends so they can perform your music. You use decibels to buy things in the virtual world of Coke Studios. You need decibels to decorate your own studio, buy furniture, pictures, etc. You can be a star, a producer, or a fan. It’s all about fun. NOTE: Before you can enter Coke Studios, you must already have or download SHOCKWAVE. Be patient, it is totally worth it. If you do not have it, Coke Music will detect this and provide the download link for you. SHOCKWAVE is free. For additional information on Coke Studios, click here to view FAQs. Back to Top Create Your Demo: Create Your Demo is a cool audio mixer that allows you to create, save, and burn a virtual CD (for use in Coke Studios) of your custom music. It’s really easy and fun. Launch it and play around with the different music genres and sounds. Back to Top Downloads: Pretty straight forward, this is where you will find music, screensavers, and wallpaper of new artists. Back to Top

text: Coke Music In order for this site to work properly you must have cookies enabled. To enable your cookies see the instructions below (Note: If your browser does not appear in the list below then consult the security/privacy and cookie settings options for your browser): PC: Internet Explorer 5.0: Click on Tools and select internet options. Select the “Security ” Tab. Click the “Custom Level” button. Scroll down unto you see the heading Cookies. In each sub-category under Cookies select that you wish to “Enable” them. Internet Explorer 6.0: Click on Tools and select internet options. Select the “Privacy” Tab. Click the “Advanced” button. Select the button for accepting cookies. Click “ok” and click “ok” again to exit the Tools section. Now you are ready to go. Netscape 6.2: Click on tasks and mouse over ”Privacy and Security” from the dropdown menu. Then Mouse over “Cookie Manager”, then select “Unblock Cookies from this Site”. Now you are ready to go. Mac : Internet Explorer 5.1: In the top navigation, select “Edit Preferences”. In the pop-up window under “Receiving Files” select and highlight “cookies”. In the screens center there is a dropdown box for “when receiving cookies:” Select the option “Never ask” and then click “OK” at the bottom to close. Now you are ready to go. Netscape 6.2.2: Click on tasks and mouse over ”Privacy and Security” from the dropdown menu. Then Mouse over “Cookie Manager”, then select “Unblock Cookies from this Site”. Now you are ready to go. Ok my cookies are enabled!

title: WHY REGISTER?
text: WHY REGISTER? Membership is the difference between a ticket and a backstage pass. When you register, you get a Coke Music Pass. It's the only way to earn decibels, play games, take surveys, register your SMS-enabled phone, and more. Only pass holders get to hang out in Coke Studios. Plus, by registering at CokeMusic.com, you will create a My Thirst ID which will enable you to gain quick access to other Coca-Cola sites.
